issues.description: Element: constructor Animal(String). In the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) the Animal(String) constructor is shown with a '-' prefix (private visibility). In the reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) the constructor is declared public (public Animal(String)). This is a real contradiction: a private constructor on Animal would prevent subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) from calling super(...), causing compilation errors if students implement the constructor as private. The UML should indicate a public or protected constructor to match the required subclassing usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML in problem_statement.md so the Animal(String) constructor is shown with public (or protected) visibility instead of private, and add a short note that subclasses must be able to call this constructor. This aligns the diagram with the implementation (public Animal(String)) and avoids student confusion and potential compilation errors.
